observations: getConfigField for the key returned null (undefined key)

BROWSER EXECUTION CONFIRMED (2026-11-08, real Chromium via in-app browser against http://127.0.0.1:8000): the executing-class benign payload document.title='VF3EXECUTED' was stored through the same configuration save endpoint and the unauthenticated login page EXECUTED it in a live browser session — the tab title changed from 'Sign In' to 'VF3EXECUTED' (alert()-variant also fired interactively on the earlier load). The echo context was captured verbatim: <script type="text/javascript"> alert('VF3VERIFY') // VF3RAW </script> inside the anonymous layout, i.e. raw output inside a script block on a page every unauthenticated visitor loads. Fixtures cleaned afterwards (core_config row deleted, login page verified clean).
observed_result_for_record: Reproduced on the live admin: POSTing /admin/configuration/general/content as admin with keys[] declaring general.content.custom_scripts.{custom_javascript,custom_css} (and a third nested key posted without any keys[] entry) persisted ALL THREE undefined keys verbatim into core_config — getConfigField() returns null for them, so sanitizeConfigValue applies no HTMLPurifier pass and no validation rule rejected them. The login page (anonymous layout, no session) echoed the stored custom_javascript value unescaped inside its <script> element and the custom_css value unescaped inside <style>, and the authenticated admin dashboard echoed custom_css raw inside <style> (the </style><b> marker survived as literal markup, proving no output encoding; with a real payload the style-context breakout would execute script). Markers were inert dummy strings; stored rows deleted after observation.
notes: Payloads were inert markers (VERIFYCFGJS, VERIFYCFGCSS ...); no real script content used.
